title: Identification of the global Verdier map with the inverse tensor–Hom comparison
statement:
Use the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions] at any of their four coefficient stages, with admissible structure morphism $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. Use the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the ordinary and exceptional adjunctions [fix-prop-adjunctions], and the projection transformation [def-exchange-projection, fix-prop-projection-formula]. Put
$$C=Ra_!K,\quad \omega=Ra^!\Lambda_s,\quad L=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega),\quad D=Ra_*L,\quad H=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\Lambda_s).$$
Write $\varepsilon_L:La^*D\to L$ and $\mu:Ra_!\omega\to\Lambda_s$ for the ordinary and exceptional counits. For each $T\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$, let $P_T:C\otimes^LT\to Ra_!(K\otimes^LLa^*T)$ be the projection map. Define the specified morphism
$$\alpha_s=\operatorname{curry}\bigl(\mu\circ Ra_!(\operatorname{ev}_{K,\omega}\circ(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L))\circ P_D\bigr):D\to H,$$
where evaluation and currying use the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-adjunctions, lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. Then $\alpha_s$ is the canonical isomorphism of [lem-sf-tensor-hom] at $(f,M,N)=(a,K,\Lambda_s)$, and is also the canonical isomorphism of [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction] at these inputs.

Let $u:\omega_{s,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_s$ denote the canonical identity-adjunction isomorphism supplied by the first assertion of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], put $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_{s,\Lambda})$ and $\rho=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,u):D_sC\to H$. If $e:D_sC\to D$ is the canonical exchange of [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] at $f=a$, then
$$e=\alpha_s^{-1}\circ\rho.$$
Let $F=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], with the tensor and unit comparisons [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor], put $c=FC$ and $c^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c,\Lambda)$, and let $\kappa:FH\to c^\vee$ be the coefficient tensor–Hom transpose of $F(\operatorname{ev}_{C,\Lambda_s})$ through these comparisons. The specified point-dualizing isomorphism $j:F(D_sC)\to c^\vee$ of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex] satisfies
$$j=\kappa\circ F\rho.$$
Let $g:c^\vee\to FD$ denote the canonical global Verdier-duality isomorphism of [thm-pod-global-verdier-duality], transported through the point-fibre identifications. Consequently this map is the specified inverse
$$g=Fe\circ j^{-1}=(\kappa\circ F\alpha_s)^{-1}.$$
At integral coefficients these formulas use the completed operations; at field coefficients they use rationalization and a common finite coefficient stage, respectively. No smooth-purity orientation or Poincare pairing occurs in these map identifications.

source.place: Steps 1–2, at the structure morphism; fix-lem-tensor-adjunction.proof.md Step 1 and lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex.proof.md identify the maps; full verification in report.md

proof.text: First check the domains of the test-object calculation. The conventions [def-pod-conventions] give separated finite-type $a$, the four coefficient stages and $K\in D^b_{ctf}$. The unit $\Lambda_s$ has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. The finite-Tor exceptional adjunction [fix-prop-adjunctions](2) puts $C=Ra_!K$ and $\omega=Ra^!\Lambda_s$ in their finite-Tor categories. At finite coefficients [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i)–(iii) puts $L=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega)$, $D=Ra_*L$, $H=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\Lambda_s)$, $La^*T$ and $K\otimes La^*T$ in these categories for every finite-Tor point test object $T$. Integrally, clause (vii) supplies internal-Hom preservation and $D^b_c=D^b_{ctf}$; [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] supplies the completed ordinary direct image of $L$. The exceptional adjunction already supplies $C$. Rationalization and common finite fields give the same memberships at the two field stages, using [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the coefficient-passage clause of stability. For a general finite-Tor $N$ on $s$, the exceptional adjunction puts $Ra^!N$ in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$; internal-Hom preservation puts $L_N=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Ra^!N)$ and $B_N=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,N)$ in the finite-Tor categories. Ordinary direct-image preservation then puts $A_N=Ra_*L_N$ in $D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$, using the integral direct-image statement and $D^b_c=D^b_{ctf}$ at the integral stage. The prescribed rationalization and common-stage constructions give these memberships at the field stages. This includes $N=\omega_s$. Thus both represented objects and the tests used below lie in the full finite-Tor point category; no site-perfectness or proper coincidence is required.

source.place: Step 1: domains of the Hom chain, with the current all-stage preservation statements

proof.text: For $N\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ put $L_N=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Ra^!N)$, $A_N=Ra_*L_N$ and $B_N=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,N)$. Use [lem-pod-hom-chain-counit-formula] with $(f,M)=(a,K)$. Its $\Phi_T^N$ is precisely the reverse, arrow by arrow, of the Hom chain defining each canonical source construction [lem-sf-tensor-hom, fix-lem-tensor-adjunction]: uncurry, precompose with $P_T^{-1}$, exceptional transpose, curry on $X$, ordinary transpose. Thus $\Phi_T^N(t)=\alpha_Nt$ for $\alpha_N=\operatorname{curry}(p_N)$ with the counit composite $p_N$ specified there. To verify the represented inverse, take $v=(\Phi_{B_N}^N)^{-1}(1_{B_N})$. Then $\alpha_Nv=1$; injectivity of $\Phi_{A_N}^N$ gives $v\alpha_N=1$, since both sides map to $\alpha_N$. Therefore the canonical isomorphisms in both source constructions are this $\alpha_N$. At $N=\Lambda_s$ its formula is exactly the displayed $\alpha_s$ in the statement. Naturality in $N$ from the new lemma gives $\alpha_{N'}A(b)=B(b)\alpha_N$ for $b:N\to N'$, where $A(b)=Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Ra^!b)$ and $B(b)=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,b)$.

source.place: Step 1, compared term by term with sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom/lem-sf-tensor-hom.proof.md Steps 1–2

proof.text: Write $w=\omega_{s,\Lambda}$ and take the identity-adjunction isomorphism $u:w\to\Lambda_s$ of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]. The structure-morphism mate in the exchange is $m=Ra^!u$ by [lem-pod-structure-identity-mate], applied to the exceptional adjunction of $a$ and the identity of $s$. The construction of [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] is the inverse tensor–Hom map at $N=w$, followed by $Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,m)$, hence is $e=A(u)\alpha_w^{-1}$. Step 2 gives $\alpha_sA(u)=\rho\alpha_w$. Cancelling the two inverse isomorphisms yields $e=\alpha_s^{-1}\rho$. The identity morphism satisfies the exceptional hypothesis by its identity adjunction in the point lemma.

source.place: Steps 1–2: compute the structure-morphism mate when a_Y is the identity

proof.text: At finite or integral coefficients put $(R,B)=(A_{E,n},(A_{E,n})_s)$ or $(\mathcal O_E,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$ and $L_RM=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$. We verify the hypotheses of [lem-pod-point-sections-reconstruction]. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\mathcal O_E$ is a principal ideal domain. Exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] makes $M\mapsto\underline M$ exact; at finite level $L_RM=\underline M$, and integrally $B$ is flat over $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] (with $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi_E)$), so $L_R$ is exact. Sections are exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Integrally [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] for $X=s$ gives $\Gamma(s,B)=C(\{*\},\mathcal O_E)=\mathcal O_E$. Multiplication by $\varpi_E^n$ is injective on $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, hence on the flat $B$, and the reduction isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] identifies its cokernel with $(A_{E,n})_s$; exact sections of $0\to B\to B\to(A_{E,n})_s\to0$ give $\Gamma(s,(A_{E,n})_s)=A_{E,n}$ through the constant-value map. By [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $c=FC=\Gamma(s,C)$ has bounded finite, resp. finitely generated, cohomology. Hence [lem-pod-point-sections-reconstruction] applies with its explicit adjunction: the unit $c\to\Gamma(s,L_Rc)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $L_Rc\in D^b_c(s,R)$, integrally $c$ has a bounded finite-projective representative $P$ with $L_RP$ a constructible representative of $L_Rc$, and the actual counit $L_Rc\to C$ is an isomorphism. We henceforth compute on $L_Rc$ (or $L_RP$) through this specified counit, rather than identifying arbitrary point sheaves with modules.

source.place: Second sentence, expanded by the sections/extension-of-scalars adjunction and the actual counit model

proof.text: At finite coefficients choose a K-flat representative of $c$ with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the one-object ringed site $R$. Apply [lem-pod-point-derived-hom-evaluation]; its hypotheses (exact $L_R$ and sections, $\Gamma(s,B)=R$) were verified in Step 4. With a K-injective resolution $B\to I$, the chain isomorphism $h\mapsto(x\mapsto h(1\otimes x))$ computes $FH\to c^\vee$ and preserves derived evaluation. On constructible inputs the tensor comparison is the specified one of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor], so this comparison is precisely its evaluation transpose $\kappa$. Integrally the perfect model $P$ of Step 4 meets [lem-pod-point-completed-evaluation]; its displayed equation gives the same conclusion for completed tensor. By the construction of the point-dualizing identification [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], $j$ is obtained by applying $R\mathcal Hom_s(C,u)$ and this coefficient-Hom comparison. Thus at both stages $j=\kappa F\rho$ as derived morphisms. Both $j$ and $F\rho$ are isomorphisms, so this specified $\kappa$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Second sentence: explicit Hom-complex comparison and evaluation normalization

proof.text: At $E$ choose the integral representative specified by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Its evaluated integral complex is perfect by [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius]; use the bounded finite-projective model $P$ of Step 4. By the construction of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex] at $E$, $j$ is the rationalized integral identification followed by the perfect scalar-Hom isomorphism $\delta$ of [lem-pc-base-change-rhom-perfect], the $E$-linear extension of $h\mapsto h\otimes1$, so on representatives $\delta(h\otimes a)=(x\otimes b\mapsto h(x)ab)$. The rational tensor comparison of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] is the balanced map on the same models, so $\kappa$ at $E$ is the transpose of $\Gamma(s,\operatorname{ev})\otimes E$; evaluating $\delta(h\otimes a)$ on $x\otimes b$ gives $h(x)ab$ with the same sign $(-1)^{pj}$, hence $\kappa_E=\delta\circ(\kappa\otimes E)$, while $F\rho$ at $E$ is $F\rho\otimes E$. Tensoring the integral equation of Step 5 with $E$ and composing with $\delta$ gives $j=\kappa F\rho$ at $E$, also when the integral representative has torsion. For a localized morphism $v\otimes a$, naturality is the integral naturality equation multiplied by $a$, and additivity handles sums. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ represent $C$ over a finite field $E$; the equation holds at that stage. For a larger finite field $L$, [lem-pod-point-scalar-hom-evaluation], applied to $P$ and its dual model, identifies the internal-Hom scalar comparison (the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation) through $\varphi$ of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] with the coefficient arrow $P^\vee\otimes_RR'\to\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_{R'}(P\otimes_RR',R')$, after rationalization and compatibly with identities and towers. Thus the representatives of both sides at $E$ and $L$ correspond, and $j=\kappa F\rho$ holds in the common finite-stage category.

source.place: Second sentence at E and algebraically closed coefficients: rationalization and common-stage evaluation calculation

proof.text:
Finally the global comparison of [thm-pod-global-verdier-duality] is constructed by applying the point functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] to the exchange $e$ and using the specified point-dualizing identification on its source. Spelling out this source construction gives $g=F(e)j^{-1}$. Substituting the equalities of Steps 3 and 5–6 and cancelling inverse isomorphisms gives
$$\begin{aligned}
g&=F(\alpha_s)^{-1}F(\rho)(\kappa F(\rho))^{-1}\\
 &=F(\alpha_s)^{-1}\kappa^{-1}=(\kappa F(\alpha_s))^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
Functoriality carries the inverse identities through $F$, and these displayed cancellations prove both inverse equations. All point identifications are the coefficient-stage ones of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]; the integral operations remain completed, and the field calculations are those of Step 6. No smooth orientation, proper-support identification or Poincare pairing enters this calculation.
